blocks.text: Managing survey data in Excel on Mac

Market research involves large datasets from platforms like Qualtrics or SurveyMonkey. You often need to clean these files before analysis. Excel for Mac handles over one million rows, but performance drops if you use too many complex formulas. Keep your data in a clean table structure. Use the Insert > Table menu to define your range. This ensures your formulas update when you add new survey responses.

Data cleaning is the most time-consuming part of your job. You often deal with inconsistent date formats or phone numbers missing leading zeros. Use the Data > Text to Columns tool to split merged survey answers. If you need to convert text strings to numbers, use the Paste Special feature to multiply by one. This forces Excel to treat the cells as numeric values.

items: Use ⌘ + Shift + L to toggle filters quickly.
Remove duplicates via Data > Remove Duplicates to clean respondent lists.
Use ⌘ + D to fill formulas down a column instantly.
Apply Data Validation to restrict inputs in survey coding sheets.

blocks.text: Keyboard shortcuts reduce the time you spend moving your mouse. On a Mac, the command key ⌘ is your best friend. Use ⌘ + T to turn a range into a formal table. To select an entire column, use ⌃ + Space. To select a full row, use ⇧ + Space. These shortcuts keep your hands on the keyboard during long analysis sessions.
If a shortcut does not work, check your System Settings under Keyboard > Shortcuts. Some Mac system commands override Excel defaults.
blocks.title: Shortcut conflicts

blocks.text: You likely use VLOOKUP or XLOOKUP to merge datasets from different survey tools. XLOOKUP is better because it searches in any direction and handles missing values better. Use COUNTIFS to calculate frequencies for multiple choice survey questions. If you need to calculate percentage change, use the simple formula (New - Old) / Old. Format these cells as percentages using ⌃ + ⇧ + %.

Charts help stakeholders understand complex data. Pivot tables are the fastest way to summarize large datasets. Use Insert > PivotTable to aggregate your survey results by demographic or region. Once you have a pivot table, use the Insert > Chart menu to add a column or bar chart. Keep your charts simple and remove unnecessary gridlines to improve readability.
How to use Lazur for market research tasks

Lazur acts as your assistant while you work in Excel. Hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask where a specific setting is. Lazur will draw a circle around the menu item. If you forget how to write a complex formula, ask Lazur to explain the syntax. It stays in the notch and waits for your next question.

Market researchers spend about 18% of their time on non-research admin work. Use Lazur to manage your calendar and email responses. Dictate your status updates using the fn key. This keeps your hands free to continue working in your spreadsheet. Avoid the 23-minute recovery cost by keeping your research tasks in one window and your communication in another.

faq.question: How do I fix leading zeros being removed in Excel?
faq.answer: Select the column, right-click, choose Format Cells, and set the category to Text before you paste your data.

faq.question: Can Lazur edit my Excel files directly?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons or edit files. It guides you through the process, points at the right menus, and explains how to perform tasks yourself.

faq.question: Is Excel for Mac the same as the Windows version?
faq.answer: It is very similar, but some advanced features like Power Query are limited or work differently. Most standard analytical functions work identically.

faq.question: Does Lazur store my screen data?
faq.answer: No. Lazur only looks at your screen while you hold the shortcut key. No screenshots or audio are stored.
